claims.hypothesis: Follow-up high-resolution ALMA Cycle 3 observations and combined Cycles 2+3 data can resolve the internal spatial structure and refine the total flux of [O III] 88 μm in SXDF-NB1006-2.
claims.experiment: Imaged Cycle 3 data at 0.14" x 0.13" resolution, performed velocity-optimized integrations, and combined Cycle 2 and Cycle 3 data with a 0.3" uv-taper.
claims.result: Detected 2-3 marginal (>3σ) clumps on scales of 0.32-0.85 kpc in Cycle 3 data and a 5.9σ total detection of 0.570 ± 0.151 Jy km s^-1 in tapered Cycles 2+3 data.
claims.finding: [O III] 88 μm emission in SXDF-NB1006-2 exhibits a clumpy structure, though interferometric noise artifacts on a smooth disk cannot be completely ruled out, and the total luminosity is 1.25 times higher than (but consistent within 1σ with) previous Cycle 2 measurements.

evidence.quote: The follow-up ALMA observations with higher angular resolution and sensitivity reveal a clumpy structure of the [O III ] emission on a scale of 0.32–0.85 kpc.

However, it is possible that a smooth disk can look clumpy in images obtained from high angular resolution interferometric observations (Gullberg et al. 2018), and we cannot rule out this possibility for our clumpy [O III ] detection.

claims.hypothesis: Combining all three ALMA cycles of [C II] 158 μm observations (Cycles 1, 3, and 7) provides a robust detection of [C II] in SXDF-NB1006-2.
claims.experiment: Adjusted visibility weights with statwt, combined Cycles 1, 3, and 7 MSs, created moment-0 maps, and tested sensitivity to a bright edge velocity bin (+120 to +145 km s^-1).
claims.result: Combined data yield a 4.5σ detection (0.100 ± 0.038 Jy km s^-1), but excluding the suspicious edge channel reduces the detection to 3.6σ (0.051 ± 0.027 Jy km s^-1), while Cycle 7 alone shows a non-detection (<0.088 Jy km s^-1).
claims.finding: [C II] 158 μm is marginally detected at 3.6σ-4.5σ, but the signal is unstable across cycles and has low robustness.

claims.hypothesis: Correcting for surface brightness dimming (SBD) brings the [O III]/[C II] luminosity ratio and L_[C II]-SFR relation of SXDF-NB1006-2 into agreement with local and z < 9 galaxy relations.
claims.experiment: Calculated observed and SBD-corrected [O III]/[C II] luminosity ratios and compared [C II] luminosities against L_[C II]-SFR relations from local starbursts, ALPINE, and z > 6 galaxies.
claims.result: [O III]/[C II] ratios are 10.2 ± 4.7 (6.1 ± 3.5 SBD-corrected) for 4.5σ and 20 ± 12 (9.6 ± 6.1 SBD-corrected) for 3.6σ; L_[C II] lies 0.6-1.3 dex below mean L_[C II]-SFR relations when using the SED-derived SFR.
claims.finding: While the SBD-corrected [O III]/[C II] luminosity ratios are consistent with the upper range of local dwarf galaxies, SXDF-NB1006-2 still exhibits a strong [C II] deficit of 0.6-1.3 dex relative to mean L_[C II]-SFR relations.

claims.hypothesis: Spectral-scan surveys using [C II] 158 μm (such as REBELS) are complete for high-SFR galaxies at z ~ 7.
claims.experiment: Analyzed the Cycle 7 REBELS [C II] observation of SXDF-NB1006-2 and compared its sensitivity limit with the galaxy's [C II] luminosity.
claims.result: [C II] was undetected in the Cycle 7 REBELS data (<0.088 Jy km s^-1 at 3σ) because the galaxy's [C II] luminosity ((0.6-1.2) x 10^8 L_sun) falls below the REBELS 5σ sensitivity limit (2-3 x 10^8 L_sun).
claims.finding: Spectral-scan surveys using [C II] are incomplete for high-z galaxies that have high SFRs but marginal [C II] emission due to the large dispersion in the L_[C II]-SFR relation.

referee_caveats_inferred: Velocity integration ranges for sub-clumps (A1, A2, B', C', C'', SE, NW) were tuned post-hoc to maximize S/N, which can artificially inflate detection significances of noise peaks.

Deconvolved source sizes measured from 3.6-4.5σ images have ~50% uncertainties (or are unconstrained along the minor axis), propagating large systematic uncertainties into the surface brightness dimming (SBD) correction factors.

Dust mass and total IR luminosity upper limits rely on a single assumed dust temperature (T_dust = 40 K) and emissivity index (β = 1.5), and explicitly omit CMB heating and contrast effects at z = 7.212.
